summary:
The patient sustained a motor vehicle accident in September 2023 that resulted in left arm fractures, requiring emergency orthopedic surgery with open reduction and internal fixation of the left humerus and radius. The patient also sustained a left knee contusion and experienced cervical spine trauma.

Imaging revealed a posterior cervical disc bulge at the C5-C6 level. Records indicate this disc abnormality may have been preexisting, documented from prior imaging following a gym weightlifting injury in 2022, though the exact timeline remains somewhat unclear in the records.

Following surgery, the patient underwent an extended course of physical therapy, initially at one facility and later transitioning to a sports medicine complex. Treatment addressed the left arm fractures, cervical strain, and associated pain through progressive exercises, manual therapy, and modalities including traction and heat application.

The patient completed approximately sixty physical therapy sessions total. Throughout rehabilitation, cervical symptoms were frequently provoked during treatment sessions, requiring ongoing modification and monitoring. The patient experienced a setback due to missed sessions early in recovery, resulting in increased stiffness that required intensive intervention to counteract.

At discharge, the left arm fractures had achieved bony union with stable hardware. However, the patient retained persistent deficits including limited forearm and shoulder range of motion and chronic cervical pain despite completion of intensive rehabilitation.
